title: BioRad Gel Doc XR+ imager
manualMd: UV / white-light gel documentation system. Captures TIFF/PNG of agarose gels stained with EtBr, GelRed, SYBR. Software: Image Lab.
locationHint: Imaging closet, near the bench-top centrifuge
hazardsMd:
- UV at 312 nm: never open the door while UV is on. The shutter interlock prevents this; if it's been bypassed, do not use.
- Ethidium-bromide stained gels are mutagenic. Wear gloves; dispose of gels as hazardous waste.

operations.title: Daily check
operations.bodyMd: Confirm the UV door interlock works. Wipe the gel tray with a damp paper towel; old EtBr residue glows on UV and ruins images.

operations.title: Capture an EtBr gel
operations.bodyMd:
1. Lay the gel flat on the UV tray (no buffer pooling).
2. Close the door fully.
3. In Image Lab, pick 'EtBr' application → Live → tune exposure (typical 0.5-2 s).
4. Capture. Save as TIFF for downstream analysis; PNG is fine for slides.

operations.title: Bands are washed out
operations.bodyMd: Exposure too long, or you stained twice. Lower exposure to 0.5 s; if still saturated, the gel was over-stained. Re-run with less stain next time.

operations.title: No bands visible
operations.bodyMd: Confirm UV is on (shutter open icon in Image Lab). If yes, the stain may have washed out — re-stain in 0.5 μg/mL EtBr for 20 min and re-image. Or your DNA didn't make it into the gel.

operations.title: Post-use
operations.bodyMd: Remove the gel to the EtBr-waste container. Wipe the tray. Save your images to the shared drive — the local cache is purged weekly. Log out of Image Lab.
